Senses.Explanation: Answering the call records the audible response after one person summons another, preserving the call-and-response sequence of the case. To answer when called or to acknowledge an instruction. The word is attested. Compilers repeatedly preserve the same audible action as the hinge of an encounter: Nanyang Huizhong calls his attendant three times and receives three answers; Shakyamuni calls Ananda after Ananda asks about the former buddhas' procedure; Mahakasyapa calls Ananda in the robe-transmission case; and Huangbo Xiyun names Pei Xiu by calling him, then declares the naming complete when Pei answers. In Xingsen's record an unnamed lecture master answers the call 'Lecturer,' and Xingsen immediately appraises him. Dahui Zonggao later raises an exchange in which Luoshan calls Zhaoqing and Zhaoqing answers before Luoshan replies 'a macaque enters the site of the Way'. The same response also acknowledges an instruction: Ananda answers Shakyamuni's order to enter the city with the bowl. The Zen bend is not a special second meaning but the records' placement of this ordinary answer as the next public turn and, at times, the central action of a named case.
